identity.title: A detailed view of the gas shell around R Sculptoris with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We analyse $^{12}\rm{CO}(1-0)$, $^{12}\rm{CO}(2-1)$, and $^{12}\rm{CO}(3-2)$ emission, observed with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) during Cycle 0 and complemented by single-dish observations.

evidence.quote: We will use 370 pc throughout this paper, noting the high uncertainty in this value.

distance_source.value: Knapp et al. 2003; Whitelock et al. 2008 (adopted, highly uncertain)

evidence.quote: We will use 370 pc throughout this paper, noting the high uncertainty in this value.

question.value: What are the mass and temperature of the gas shell around R Scl, and how did the mass-loss rate evolve during and after the thermal pulse?

evidence.quote: We aim to determine the physical properties of the detached gas shell around R Sculptoris, in particular the shell mass and temperature, and to constrain the evolution of the mass-loss rate during and after a thermal pulse.
This paper makes use of ALMA data from project no. ADS/ JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00131.S.
The main target of the observations were the $^{12}\rm{CO}(1-0)$ line in Band 3, the $^{12}\rm{CO}(2-1)$ line in Band 6, and the $^{12}\rm{CO}(3-2)$ line in Band 7.
Observations of the $^{12}\rm{CO}(1-0)$ emission line at 115.27 GHz were carried out between Jan 23 and Jan 25 2012.
Observations of the $^{12}\rm{CO}(2-1)$ emission line at 230.54 GHz were carried out on Oct 1 2011.
Observations of the $^{12}\rm{CO}(3-2)$ emission line at 345.80 GHz were carried out between Oct 3 and Oct 19 2011.

configurations.value: Cycle 0 compact configuration of the main array, pointed mosaics; no ACA

evidence.quote: R Scl was observed during ALMA Cycle 0 using the compact configuration of the main array.

observing_dates.value: Band 3: Jan 23-25 2012; Band 6: Oct 1 2011; Band 7: Oct 3-19 2011

evidence.quote: Observations of the $^{12}\rm{CO}(2-1)$ emission line at 230.54 GHz were carried out on Oct 1 2011.

We assume a fractional abundance of $^{12}$CO of f($^{12}$CO)=$4.3\times10^{-4}$ relative to H$_2$ (cite: olofssonetal1993a).

findings_qualitative.value: The shell is entirely filled with gas, not detached

evidence.loc: 2.4 Interferometer vs. single-dish observations and extended emission
evidence.quote: Extended emission from $^{12}$CO reaching out to the shell means that the shell is in fact not detached, but instead filled with significant amounts of molecular gas.

evidence.quote: However, it is not clear what the origin of this higher-velocity component is.
